result: I built `index.html` as a single-page, CSS-only cinematic experience with no JavaScript at all, so the "works with JS disabled" constraint is trivially satisfied and every animation lives behind `@supports` and `prefers-reduced-motion` guards that fall back to fully static, fully visible content. The visual concept follows the tagline literally: a fixed full-bleed gradient backdrop drifts from pale flour-cream at the top through crust-amber to deep tide-teal at the bottom, using `animation-timeline: scroll(root)` where supported, so scrolling the page reads like moving from the shop's morning light down into the river at dusk; sections also get a subtle CSS `animation-timeline: view()` fade-up as they enter, again with static fallback. Typography pairs a warm serif (Georgia) for headings/quotes with system sans for body copy to feel handmade rather than corporate, and all imagery — the ferry-hall silhouette, tide lines, and the four loaf/crumpet illustrations — is hand-drawn inline SVG so nothing is fetched externally. Layout uses fluid `clamp()` type scales and an auto-fit grid for the loaves so it holds up cleanly from 390px (stacked, nav links collapse to just the Subscribe pill) to 1440px (multi-column) without fixed widths or overflow, and every word of copy is used verbatim from the brief, including the CTA as a `mailto:` link.
